svg.title: Pooled variance contains within-group and between-group variation
svg.desc: Group A contains three, three, seven and seven: count four, mean five and population variance four. Group B contains eight, eight, eight, twelve, twelve and twelve: count six, mean ten and population variance four. Every repeated observation is drawn separately on a shared horizontal scale. Triangles mark the group means. The dashed line is the pooled mean eight, obtained by dividing total eighty by count ten. The within-group contribution is four tenths of four plus six tenths of four, equal to four. The between-group contribution is four tenths of five minus eight squared plus six tenths of ten minus eight squared, equal to six. Pooled variance is ten, not four. The pooled standard deviation is the square root of ten. Both groups measure the same numerical quantity.
